thread.title: How to merge multiple data tables with specific conditionals on NA's

author: road_to_quantdom
title: How to merge multiple data tables with specific conditionals on NA's
text:
I have data.table 's that are in this format:
dt1 <- data.table(row_names=1:5,perf=c(2,NA,NA,3,NA),ticker=rep("aa",5)) dt2 <- data.table(row_names=1:5,perf=c(NA,1,2,5,NA),ticker=rep("aapl",5)) row_names perf ticker 1: 1 2 aa 2: 2 NA aa 3: 3 NA aa 4: 4 3 aa 5: 5 NA aa row_names perf ticker 1: 1 NA aapl 2: 2 1 aapl 3: 3 2 aapl 4: 4 5 aapl 5: 5 NA aapl
I have N of these data tables and would like to join them so that I take the average of perf . However, I do not want to do this if an NA value exists for one of the data tables. In the case above, I would like the resulting data.table
> res <- data.table(row_names=1:5,perf=c(2,1,2,4,NA),tickers=c("aa","aapl","aapl","aa,aapl",NA)) > res row_names perf tickers 1: 1 2 aa 2: 2 1 aapl 3: 3 2 aapl 4: 4 4 aa,aapl 5: 5 NA NA
I know I could do something like this to get the means with NA 's removed:
rbind(dt1,dt2)[,list("perf"=mean(perf,na.rm=T)),by=row_names]
row_names perf 1: 1 2 2: 2 1 3: 3 2 4: 4 4 5: 5 NaN
How would I go about setting the conditions for the tickers column to paste them based on the conflicting NA 's. Also, is rbinding all the data tables the most efficient way to perform the mean function? Thank you!
